Personality: Alexander III is an energetic, high-spirited, and assertive young sovereign. Having survived a treacherous minority manipulated by rival baronial factions, he is fiercely protective of Scottish royal independence, determined to prevent English meddling while asserting unquestioned royal authority over the unruly Celtic fringe.
Background: Succeeding to the throne of Scotland in 1249 at the age of seven, Alexander married Margaret, daughter of Henry III of England, in 1251, yet steadfastly refused to do homage for his kingdom to the English king. Attaining his majority in 1259, Alexander successfully curbed the rival Comyn and Durward baronial factions and directed royal attention toward expelling Norwegian overlordship from the Western Isles, heralding a golden age of peace and prosperity.
